title: Calculator App
story: Every phone has one. Every computer has one. Now YOU build one. A calculator with add, subtract, multiply, divide — plus memory (store/recall/clear) and calculation history. This is the program that launched a thousand programming careers.
why: A calculator app combines arithmetic operations, state management (memory, history), match for operation selection, and Vec for history — a polished utility program.
analogy: A desk calculator with paper tape: the display shows the current number, memory stores a number for later, and the tape records every calculation. Your calculator app has a display (current_value), a memory slot, and a tape (Vec history). Press C to clear, M+ to store.
try_it: Add more operations: power (x^y), percentage (x% of y), square root, sign flip (+/-). Add 'undo' that reverses the last operation using history. Implement BigDecimal-like precision for floating-point. Add parentheses and order-of-operations to handle '2 + 3 * 4' correctly.
tips: Track history in a Vec — each entry contains the operation and result
Memory is just a separate stored value — simple but powerful
Every operation updates current_value and pushes to history
common_mistakes: Not checking for division by zero — the classic calculator crash
Allowing operations to overflow without detection
History growing unbounded — consider capping at last N entries
